title: .NET 11 Preview 6 Modernises MAUI CollectionView and Android Shell
gist: .NET 11 Preview 6 continues Microsoft's replacement of Xamarin.Forms-era MAUI internals with handlers and source generators: CollectionView2 lands on Windows via WinUI ItemsRepeater, Android Shell moves to the handler model, HybridWebView interop drops reflection to unblock Native AOT, and the Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility package is removed as a breaking change for legacy Xamarin dependents.

insights.claim: The .NET 11 cycle is explicitly about replacing Xamarin.Forms-era infrastructure in MAUI with platform handlers and source-generated code, with earlier previews already making the XAML source generator the default.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Microsoft is finally retiring the acquired-Xamarin architecture; MAUI's reliability trajectory depends on how completely this lands.

insights.claim: Preview 6 removes the Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility NuGet package, a potentially breaking change forcing projects that reference it or its Xamarin.Forms compatibility renderers to migrate before targeting .NET 11.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: A hard migration deadline for legacy Xamarin codebases - a concrete driver of mobile-development consulting and rewrite spend.
insights.locator: One potentially breaking change is the removal

insights.claim: Applications that reference only Microsoft.Maui.Controls are unaffected by the removal because several compatibility-named base types remain in the core assembly, limiting the blast radius to explicit dependents.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Narrows who actually has to act - the breaking change is targeted, not ecosystem-wide.
insights.locator: Regular applications that reference only Microsoft.Maui.Controls

insights.claim: CollectionView2 (CV2), the next-generation list implementation, has arrived on Windows using WinUI's ItemsRepeater, bringing Windows in line with the CV2 implementations already shipping on Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Cross-platform parity on the most-used and most-complained-about MAUI control is a prerequisite for enterprise adoption at scale.
insights.locator: The largest UI change is the arrival of CollectionView2

insights.claim: The new Windows handler maps MAUI linear and grid layouts onto virtualising WinUI layouts and supports grouping, selection, headers and footers, empty views, snapping, incremental loading, and RefreshView integration.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Virtualisation plus incremental loading is what makes data-heavy line-of-business apps viable on MAUI Windows.
insights.locator: It maps MAUI linear and grid layouts

insights.claim: Shell on Android is reimplemented on standard MAUI handlers, with new ShellHandler, ShellItemHandler and ShellSectionHandler classes replacing renderer-based ones and reusing components shared with FlyoutViewHandler and TabbedPage.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Consolidating navigation onto shared handler components reduces long-run platform-specific bug surface in MAUI's navigation stack.
insights.locator: Preview 6 also reimplements Shell on Android

insights.claim: The Shell rework is Android-only for now while iOS and Mac Catalyst keep their existing Shell renderers, so apps with custom Shell behaviour or renderer-level dependencies face a divergent, test-heavy migration.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Platform divergence during a multi-release migration is where regression risk and upgrade cost concentrate for MAUI shops.
insights.locator: Microsoft describes this as an Android-only change

insights.claim: HybridWebView JavaScript interop now uses a source generator instead of reflection, removing trimming and AOT warnings and letting the control work in fully trimmed and Native AOT applications.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Reflection removal is the gating dependency for Native AOT mobile apps - watch it as the path to smaller binaries and faster startup.
insights.locator: For hybrid applications, HybridWebView JavaScript interop

insights.claim: On Android, MAUI now filters incoming JavaScript messages by source so unrelated window.postMessage events, such as those from nested frames, are no longer surfaced as native messages.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Closes a hybrid-app trust boundary where nested-frame content could inject into the native bridge.
insights.locator: On Android, MAUI also filters incoming JavaScript messages

insights.claim: Android applications gain opt-in MediaPicker result recovery, with new APIs to retrieve, wait for, or clear media results when Android terminates and recreates the app process while the system camera or picker is still open.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Addresses a long-standing Android process-death data-loss failure mode that silently breaks capture flows in production apps.
insights.locator: Android applications also gain opt-in MediaPicker result recovery

insights.claim: A new MinimumDistance property on GeolocationListeningRequest lets apps request location notifications only after the device has moved a specified number of meters.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Small but battery-relevant - movement-gated location callbacks reduce power draw in tracking-heavy apps.
insights.locator: The release adds a MinimumDistance property

insights.claim: Apple workloads in Preview 6 now target stable Xcode 26.6 and .NET for Android aligns HTTP failure and cancellation behaviour more closely with the broader HttpClient contract.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Toolchain stabilisation on stable Xcode is what makes a preview usable for teams shipping to the App Store on current SDKs.
insights.locator: Apple workloads now target stable Xcode 26.6
